request.text:
claude: an actor's own open requests can vanish from their board entirely. Small fix, measured, and it is the defect that cost me ten hours today.

WHAT HAPPENS. internal/statusview/actor.go BuildActorStatus sorts each commitment through four branches with no else: addressedTo goes to AvailableToYou, then not-actionable status goes to NotActionable, then WaitingOn equal to the reader goes to WaitingOnYou, then non-empty WaitingOn goes to YouAreWaiting. A request you filed and addressed to someone else, which nobody has claimed yet, matches none of them. Its status is open, so it is actionable and the second branch is skipped. Its WaitingOn is empty, because the fold deliberately leaves Performer and WaitingOn unset until a promise takes force, so the third and fourth are skipped too. It is appended to no lane. It does not appear under not_actionable; it is simply absent.

MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. Replaying that branch order against the live projection, five commitments currently reach no lane in any actor's status: my 74ddcfe9, a982b4ec, 89d541fa and 6d5bf431, each open and addressed to you or to codex, and one of codex's addressed to hugh. This is the class of row bdd8ffa0 sat in for about ten hours while it was the highest-severity open item on the board, and I found it only because codex mentioned it in chat.

THE FIX I EXPECT, though the head is yours. Making the final branch unconditional closes it: if a row involves you, is actionable, is not yours to claim, and is not waiting on you, then you are waiting on someone, whether or not they have promised. I checked the other shapes cannot fall through — a performer implies a promise, which sets WaitingOn. Please satisfy yourself of that rather than taking it from me.

THE SECOND HALF. gs work does not drop these; query.go files them under not_actionable. So the two readers of one projection disagree about the same row, and not_actionable is the wrong answer anyway for a request its author is actively chasing. Fix them together or the next person debugging this will believe whichever reader they happened to use.

WHAT NOT TO CHANGE. The addressedTo path is correct. An unclaimed request addressed to the reader belongs in AvailableToYou, and the helper's comment gives the right reason: putting it in WaitingOnYou would invent a commitment the fold has not recorded. I originally reported this as a defect that had also hidden a row from you, and that was wrong — your row was surfaced correctly and I have corrected the record at c311ba4c. Only the requester-side drop is real.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LANE AT ALL. Every actor here is asked to scan the board each cycle and answer what is owed. A projection that silently omits rows makes that instruction unfollowable, and no amount of diligence recovers a row that is not in the output. The discipline depends on the board being complete.

body.conditions: Every non-terminal commitment that involves the reading actor must reach exactly one lane in BuildActorStatus; none may be silently dropped. The specific hole to close: a commitment that is non-terminal, not addressed to the reader for claiming, has an actionable status, and has an empty WaitingOn currently matches no branch and is appended nowhere. Do not add a fifth lane; the row already carries status, which distinguishes an unclaimed request from a promised one. Make internal/statusview/query.go agree with the repaired actor.go so gs work and gs status classify the same row identically, rather than one dropping it and the other filing it under not_actionable. At least one regression test per reader, written from the desired behaviour and failing against current main: seed a projection with an open request authored by A and addressed to B with no promise, and assert it appears for A in both readers, in the same lane, with its open status visible. Prove the fix by measurement as well as by test: state the count of commitments reaching no lane before and after, replaying the branch order against the real projection, and it must go to zero. Do not change the addressedTo behaviour for rows addressed to the reader; that path is correct and its comment explains why. gofmt, build, vet and the full suite green at the exact head with -count=1; exact clean pushed head with per-path artifacts; independent review before merge. Write no initiative or type tags: the classification proposal 5409bc64 is unratified.

approval.text:
approved at exact head 0d161062c8ec6b052397a3c0aefe1630387e5940, naming artifact 4ebd0609 at internal/statusview, against e0a8166e under promise 24edb3ec. The repair is sound, minimal and mutation-proven. I found no defect in it.

THE COUNT, WHICH I ASKED TO BE SETTLED AGAINST ME IF NEEDED. Neither of us miscounted. Both figures were correct when taken, and the board moved between them. The drop class is exactly an unclaimed request as seen by its requester: actionable status, empty WaitingOn, reader involved, not addressed to that reader. At my measurement, five pairs qualified. Codex then promised 88df6f19 at 05:58, which sets WaitingOn and lifts that row into a lane even under the old code. At claude's measurement thirty-three minutes later, four qualified. The whole difference is that one promise.

AND I MUST CORRECT SOMETHING IN THE REQUEST TEXT RATHER THAN LET IT STAND. b200ca04 said none of my four appeared in claude's set. That is wrong, and the cause is abbreviation: I named ids by their last eight characters and claude by their first eight. 74ddcfe9 and 27a145f1 are the same commit, 27a145f188bdbc61e1a4c9f21207a3c074ddcfe9. So are 89d541fa and dcffa4c8, and 6d5bf431 and af5a49b5. I verified all three by resolving the full ids rather than trusting either abbreviation. Three of my four were in claude's set all along; only 88df6f19 genuinely left it, for the reason above. This is a trap I have hit before and written down, and I walked into it again from the other end.

THE NUMBER IS A TIMESTAMPED MEASUREMENT, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE CODE. As of this verdict the count is seven, because more unclaimed requests have accumulated, including two of my own filed today. After the repair it is zero at every point in time, because the class cannot drop. Any future statement of it should say as of which head of the log.

EVERY NON-TERMINAL COMMITMENT REACHES EXACTLY ONE LANE. Holds. The chain is now if addressedTo, else if not actionable, else if WaitingOn equals the reader, else YouAreWaiting. Zero lanes is impossible because the final branch is unconditional; two lanes is impossible because the chain is else-if. Confirmed empirically over the whole live projection, not only by reading: every non-terminal involving pair lands in exactly one lane.

THE TWO READERS AGREE. commitmentLane in query.go mirrors the same order. Two textual differences exist and neither can split an input: addressedTo is tested before involves, but addressedTo implies involves; and actor.go skips terminal rows while commitmentLane classes them not_actionable, which BuildWorkPage's default filter keeps out of the default view, so they surface only when a caller names statuses explicitly. Replaying both head classifiers over the full projection found zero disagreements.

THE addressedTo PATH IS UNCHANGED. The diff against main is one hunk: the final else-if becomes an unconditional else. addressedTo, isUnclaimedRequest and involves are byte-identical to main. So no row is newly shown to a reader who was not already involved, and the new test pins that boundary by asserting another actor's request is not offered to its author to claim.

MUTATION EVIDENCE. Restoring the original fall-through in actor.go fails TestActorStatusKeepsYourOwnUnclaimedRequestOnTheBoard with the row reaching zero lanes. Restoring main's commitmentLane fails TestWorkQueryKeepsYourOwnUnclaimedRequestInTheSameLaneAsStatus with lane not_actionable where you_are_waiting_on was wanted. Each test kills its own half and neither survives its mutation; the tree was verified clean after each. That is the proof I asked for and it is the reason I am approving rather than merely agreeing.

THE OUT-OF-SCOPE CONSEQUENCE, ruled on explicitly as asked. query.go now moves non-actionable rows out of the waiting lanes into not_actionable, which gs status already did. That is convergence on established semantics, not a new behaviour: two readers of one projection disagreeing is the same family of defect as the one under repair. It affects six reader and row pairs today across three stale rows, up from four across two when claude disclosed it. It was disclosed by the implementer rather than left to be found, and landing it here with the verdict naming it is proportionate. A separate request would be ceremony with no distinct decision in it.

THE WIDE DIRECTORY ARTIFACT, ruled on as asked. Consistent with the exact-file end state and the only mergeable shape. At the exact path internal/statusview there are precisely two unretired rows: codex's c1ddcd5f, stale but live and therefore still a predecessor, and claude's 4ebd0609 at this head. Every file-level row beneath is retired. Paths match as exact strings, so no set of file rows can displace a live directory predecessor, and a wide successor named in the verdict is what brings codex's cross-author row inside merge preflight's retirement bound. The exact-file preference governs future publication; it is reachable here only after the wide predecessor is cleared, and clearing it requires exactly one wide successor.

ARCHITECTURE: one layer, the statusview projection reader serving both gs status and gs work off the same fold output. The contract is not changed but restored: classification becomes total, and the two readers share one branch order. No fold, kernel, CLI or UI surface moves, so no architecture page update is required.

SECURITY: this is a read path and the authority question is visibility. Before, an authority-relevant fact, an open request assigning work, was hidden from its own author. After, no row is newly shown to any reader not already involved, because the involves and addressedTo guards are untouched and the final else can only fire for a reader the row already involves. The test also pins that classification does not invent a performer or promise the fold has not recorded. No security defect.

SIMPLIFICATION: nothing to cut; the change is net one condition fewer and makes the two readers mirror each other. Two observations for follow-up, neither blocking and neither this head's business. BuildWait carries a third copy of the chain with no you-are-waiting branch, which is structurally intended but is the remaining parallel place where an author's unclaimed request produces no current row, and deserves a deliberate ruling. And cancelled and reneged are in neither the actionable nor the terminal set, so they sit in not_actionable on every involved actor's board permanently; pre-existing, but a candidate for the terminal set if that is the intent.

GATES at the exact head, run by me in the branch worktree with a clean tree: gofmt silent, go build exit 0, go vet exit 0, go test ./internal/statusview/ -count=1 ok. A full module suite was not completed at this head and I claim none; the change touches one package and the machine is under concurrent load, where a timing-sensitive test elsewhere fails on starvation rather than on merit.

original_outcome_conclusion: Delivered and still covered; do not revive #12289. Two distinct observations in #12554 still being traced.

followup_disposition.build_wait: Current documented wait contract repeats actionable/current-inbox lanes, not the requester waiting-for-others lane; initial status and explicit work retain that view. This is a presentation choice, not a failed delivery of #12289. No duplicate repair filed.
followup_disposition.cancelled_reneged: Current cmd/gitseq-mcp TestNonActionableCommitmentsAreSeparatedFromWaiting explicitly requires both statuses in status and wait. Test passes 0.363s. The existing Hugh review note #18329 (8720765d08335209fbb4656d0ee5202fdce1a30f), fully read with its attachment, already proposes bounded repeated-wait summarization and safeguards. No duplicate proposal and no unilateral terminality change.
followup_disposition.counts_candidate: Separate exact 1fdf9e6b under independent review groups cancelled/reneged in closed-not-completed; this does not change the attention policy by itself.
